newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Feb 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Feb 19.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Wednesday:
WASHINGTON - A consulting firm has found that D.C. police would be able to fight crime better if Mayor Marion Barry had less power over the department and the police chief had more.
FREDERICK, Md. - A scientist who won a Nobel Prize studying disease in far-off lands admitted in court that he sexually abused a boy he brought back to Maryland from Micronesia.

WASHINGTON - Under federal law, the D.C. government must provide special education for eligible children but if the public system cannot meet their needs, as too often happens, it must pay to send students to private schools that have the services.

WASHINGTON - Some donors who wrote sizable checks last year to a national campaign committee headed by Sen. Alfonse D'Amato thought they were giving money to help elect Republican Senate candidates across the country but a lot of the money was diverted to state and local races.
WASHINGTON - Former ambassador Pamela Harriman, in a will that she signed only one month before her death, left the bulk of her estate to be divided between her only son and his estranged wife.

WASHINGTON - Three major broadcast companies -- Evergreen Media Corp., Chancellor Broadcasting Co., and Viacom Inc. -- agreed to merge their 11 Washington-area radio stations into a single new company.
